sections.h2: Where is the Stokes County Register of Deeds office?
sections.html:
It is at 1014 Main Street in Danbury, North Carolina 27016, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 67. The county lists the office phone as (336) 593-2414 and a fax at (336) 593-9360.

Office hours are 8:30 to 5:00 Monday through Friday. The county posts a shorter window for recording, 8:30 to 4:45, so a deed that arrives at 4:50 may wait until the next business day. The Tax Administration office shares the same Administration Building address, which helps because a deed here needs a tax certification first.

sections.h2: What does the office do for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
The register maintains, preserves, indexes and provides access to the county's land and vital records, and your deed becomes part of that record when it is filed. Stokes County was carved out of the eastern half of Surry County in 1789, so older deeds in this area may trace back to Surry's records, which begin in 1771.

For a sale, three tasks run through this office:

  • Recording the deed that transfers the property to the buyer.
  • Recording the new deed of trust if the buyer has a loan.
  • Recording a satisfaction so your old loan comes off the index.

sections.h2: Does a Stokes County deed need a tax clearance before recording?
sections.html:
Yes. The Stokes County Tax Administration page states that deeds submitted for recording must include a certification from Tax Administration that no delinquent taxes are owed on the real property being transferred, citing G.S. 161-31.

The practical effect is simple. If your parcel has a past-due bill, the deed will not go on record until the balance is cleared. Walk down the hall to the tax office, or have your closing attorney do it, well before the closing date. The Tax Administration office lists hours of 8:30 am to 5:00 pm, Monday through Friday.

sections.h2: What fees and taxes apply when a deed is recorded in Stokes County?
sections.html:
The amounts are set by statute for the whole state. The table shows what the statutes print.

Fees and tax a Stokes County deed filing is measured against
ItemStatutory figure
Ordinary instrument, 15 pages$26.00, then $4.00 for each extra page
Mortgage or deed of trust, 35 pages$64.00, then $4.00 for each extra page
Releases of a deed of trustNo recording fee
Plat$21.00 per sheet
Certified copy$5.00 first page plus $2.00 each added page
Deed excise tax$1.00 on each $500.00 or fractional part of value

The seller pays the excise tax to the register before the deed is recorded. Call (336) 593-2414 to ask how the office takes payment.

sections.h2: How does recording protect a Stokes County buyer or seller?
sections.html:
Under G.S. 47-18, a conveyance is not effective against a lien creditor or a buyer who gave value until it is registered in the county where the land is. Priority follows the time of registration.

A seller benefits too. Once the buyer's deed is on record, claims that arise from the buyer afterward no longer reach back to you. Ask for the recording information on your file copy so you can show the date and time later if a question comes up.

sections.h2: What other county offices do Stokes County sellers deal with?
sections.html:
Tax Administration is the first call. Its director's office accepts listing, extension and payment questions, and the department lists a P.O. Box 57 mailing address at the same Danbury building. Property record cards and land and home values sit on the county's tax website.

The county also runs a GIS site for parcel lookups, a planning department for permits and a veterans services office. A buyer or seller can use these to confirm parcel lines before a sale, particularly for rural tracts where the acreage on an old deed may differ from the current map.

sections.h2: What if the house is inherited, vacant or needs repairs?
sections.html:
Recording still ends the deal, but the pieces before it get harder. Heirs may need to settle who can sign, and a vacant house can fall behind on taxes that must be cleared before the deed can be filed.

Contact the register's office with questions about document form, and a North Carolina attorney for title questions. A buyer who purchases as-is can help when the house needs work, as long as the tax certification and recording steps still happen in order.

sections.h2: What other recording fees might show up on a Stokes County filing?
sections.html:
State law adds a few smaller charges. A document that does not meet the recording standards carries a $25.00 nonstandard add-on, and each additional instrument folded into one filing costs $10.00. The statute calls the fee schedule complete and exclusive and says fees are collected before filing, so the office cannot add its own charges.

Copies matter for a sale as well. A certified copy of a recorded deed costs $5.00 for the first page and $2.00 for each added page, which is useful if your lender or buyer's attorney asks for one. Ask the Stokes office whether it takes checks, cash or cards before you go.

sections.h2: How are contracts for deed recorded in Stokes County?
sections.html:
North Carolina Chapter 47H covers seller-financed contracts for one to four family homes where the seller keeps title and the buyer makes five or more payments beyond a down payment. The seller must record the contract, or a memorandum of it, within five business days.

The buyer can cancel until midnight of the third business day after signing. If a buyer defaults, the seller must give written notice with a cure date at least 30 days after service. For anyone who sold on a land contract in Stokes County years ago, the Register of Deeds is where the recorded memorandum should sit, so check that it was filed.

sections.h2: What should a Stokes County seller bring on recording day?
sections.html:
Your closing attorney normally files for you, but a seller who is organizing paperwork can use this short list.

  • The signed, notarized deed in recordable form.
  • Proof from Tax Administration that no delinquent tax is owed.
  • The excise tax amount, calculated from the sale price at $1.00 for each $500.00 or fractional part.
  • Payment for the recording fee, with extra for added pages.
  • A return address so the original comes back to the right person.

Record before the office's 4:45 pm recording cutoff, since the county posts that as the last time documents are taken.

sections.h2: How do I look up what is already recorded on a Stokes County parcel?
sections.html:
The county runs a GIS site for parcels and a tax website with property record cards and land and home values. Start with those to confirm the parcel number, acreage and owner name, then check the Register of Deeds for the deed chain and any unreleased deed of trust.

Because Stokes County was formed in 1789 from the eastern half of Surry, very old deeds for land near the county line may be recorded in Surry County. If the title search reaches back before 1789, the Surry County Register of Deeds is the likely place to look.

faqs.q: What are the Stokes County Register of Deeds hours?
faqs.a: The county lists office hours of 8:30 to 5:00 Monday through Friday, with recording accepted from 8:30 to 4:45.

faqs.q: Where do I mail documents to the Stokes County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: P.O. Box 67, Danbury, NC 27016. The street address is 1014 Main Street, Danbury.

faqs.q: Do I need a tax certification to record a deed in Stokes County?
faqs.a: Yes. Tax Administration must certify that no delinquent taxes are owed on the real property before a deed is submitted for recording.

faqs.q: How much is the NC deed excise tax in Stokes County?
faqs.a: The statute prints $1.00 on each $500.00 or fractional part of the consideration or value, and the seller pays it before the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to record a satisfaction of a deed of trust in Stokes County?
faqs.a: No. State law sets no fee for recording satisfactions or cancellations of deeds of trust or mortgages.
